concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a new topical family (xattr:) per the naming convention's own example; fills the round's stated gap that extended attributes are absent entirely from the registry. Application-defined metadata visible only to its creator application by default

concepts.label: virtual extended attribute (VXATTR)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sibling of xattr:extended-attribute, but server-defined rather than application-defined

concepts.label: $document virtual extended attribute

concepts.label: $XTOC virtual extended attribute
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - named VXATTR returning the list of a document's extended attribute names

relations.subject: xattr:extended-attribute
relations.evidence: This is achieved by extensions to the _Sub-Document_ API (see [Sub-Documents](data.md#sub-documents-overview)).

relations.subject: xattr:extended-attribute
relations.evidence: Extended attributes can be formed only as JSON, but can be applied to both JSON and binary items.

relations.subject: xattr:extended-attribute
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate captures per-creator visibility isolation; this is a narrower, ownership-based access model distinct from every RBAC-style requiresPrivilege/requiresRole predicate already in the registry, which gate by role rather than by 'whoever created this'
relations.evidence: However, no other application has knowledge of the extended attributes within a document other than their creator; unless such knowledge is shared explicitly between applications by some mechanism external to Couchbase Server.

relations.subject: service:search-service
relations.evidence: They are not intended for use in general applications, and data stored there cannot be accessed easily by some Couchbase services, such as Search.

relations.subject: xattr:extended-attribute
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate expresses 'the subject's size is counted against the object's overall size cap'; this is the direct answer to why a document's 20MB limit (data.md) is affected by attributes some applications cannot even see
relations.evidence: Extended attributes count against this size-limit: consequently, the size of a document may reflect the presence of data inaccessible to some applications.

relations.subject: xattr:virtual-extended-attribute
relations.evidence: A _virtual_ extended attribute is server-defined, and exposes additional information about a document.

relations.subject: xattr:document-vxattr
relations.evidence: Couchbase Server provides the virtual extended attribute, `$document`, which, when specified as a search-path, returns metadata on the document.

relations.subject: xattr:xtoc-vxattr
relations.evidence: Couchbase Server also provides the virtual extended attribute, `$XTOC`, which, when specified as a search-path, returns a list of the extended attributes for the document.

notable_absence.finding: This page never mentions RBAC, a role, or a privilege of any kind, even though scopes-and-collections.md (this batch's page 3) explicitly states that 'Access to scopes and collections is protected by Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)'. Extended attribute isolation is instead described purely as creator-application knowledge ('no other application has knowledge of the extended attributes within a document other than their creator') - a fundamentally different, non-RBAC access model living inside the same product as the RBAC system scopes-and-collections.md describes, with no page connecting the two or stating how (or whether) an RBAC privilege check ever applies to XATTR access.

cross_component_finding: The stated exclusion ('data stored there cannot be accessed easily by some Couchbase services, such as Search') means the already-promoted search:full-text-index (the index artifact fed by DCP, per its registry definition) is built over an incomplete view of a document's full metadata footprint - any application-specific XATTR data is invisible to full-text indexing by design. No page in the registry previously stated a boundary on what DCP-fed indexing actually sees; this is the first.
cross_product_finding: The only cross-product link on this page points to the Java SDK's own xattr concept docs ('[extended attributes](#3.4@java-sdk:concept-docs:xattr.adoc)'), confirming XATTRs are exposed identically through the SDK layer. Left as an open, unconfirmed question rather than asserted: whether Sync Gateway's own internal sync metadata (governed by the registry's sgw:document/sgw:channel concepts) is itself implemented using this same Couchbase Server XATTR mechanism under the hood - plausible given Sync Gateway sits on top of Couchbase Server, but no page read in this batch or earlier rounds states it, so no relation is minted for it.
